test_cases.test_name: Functional Test: X-bar/R Chart Creation and Nelson Rules Application
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can correctly create X-bar/R control charts from a CSV file and accurately apply the vendor's standard Nelson rules to identify out-of-control points.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed and accessible
Test CSV file with at least 100 data points organized in subgroups is available
User account with 'Analyst' role permissions is created and logged in

test_steps.action: Navigate to the 'New Chart' section and select 'X-bar/R Chart' as the chart type.
test_steps.expected_result: System displays the X-bar/R chart configuration interface with data import options.

test_steps.action: Upload the prepared test CSV file using the standard CSV import function.
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully loads the CSV data and populates the data preview pane without errors.

test_steps.action: Configure the chart by mapping the CSV columns to the appropriate data fields (e.g., subgroup identifier, measurement values).
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the column mappings and displays a preview of the control chart.

test_steps.action: Enable the 'Nelson Rules' option from the analysis settings and generate the final chart.
test_steps.expected_result: System renders the complete X-bar/R chart with control limits and visually highlights any points that violate the enabled Nelson rules.
data_to_capture: List of any flagged out-of-control points

test_steps.action: Verify the calculated control limits and the flagged points against manual calculations for a sample of the data.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's calculated control limits and rule violations match the expected manual calculations.

acceptance_criteria: X-bar and R charts are generated successfully from the CSV input.
Vendor's standard Nelson rules are applied correctly, and violations are clearly indicated.
All chart calculations (means, ranges, control limits) are accurate when compared to manual verification.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 211.68: Requires automated equipment to perform intended functions accurately and reliably.
General GAMP principles for verifying standard software functionality meets user requirements.
data_integrity_requirements: The original data from the CSV must be processed and displayed without alteration.
Chart calculations must be accurate and reproducible.
urs_requirements: URS-020-001: Users shall create X-bar/R and p-charts from CSV inputs.
URS-020-002: Users shall apply vendor's standard Nelson rules.

test_cases.test_name: Performance Test: Data Loading and Chart Rendering Speed
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard meets the performance requirements for loading a large dataset and rendering charts within the specified time limits.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed on supported hardware
A CSV test file containing exactly 100,000 data points is prepared
A stopwatch or system timer is available for measurement

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard and navigate to the data import screen.
test_steps.expected_result: Data import screen loads successfully and is ready for file selection.
data_to_capture: Time to load the import screen (baseline)

test_steps.action: Initiate the import of the 100,000-point CSV file and start the timer simultaneously.
test_steps.expected_result: System begins processing the file and displays a progress indicator.
data_to_capture: Start time of the import process

test_steps.action: Stop the timer when the system indicates the data import is complete and the data is ready for charting.
test_steps.expected_result: Data is fully loaded into the system's memory and available for analysis within 5 seconds.
data_to_capture: End time of the import process

test_steps.action: Configure a standard X-bar chart using the loaded dataset and apply a simple filter (e.g., filter by a specific date range).
test_steps.expected_result: Chart configuration is accepted by the system.

test_steps.action: Initiate the chart rendering and start the timer. Stop the timer when the chart is fully displayed on the screen.
test_steps.expected_result: The chart is rendered and completely visible to the user within 2 seconds after applying the filter.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 4 and 5 two more times with different filter criteria to ensure consistent performance.
test_steps.expected_result: All subsequent chart renders after filter changes are completed within the 2-second requirement.

acceptance_criteria: The 100,000 data points are loaded from the CSV file in less than 5 seconds.
Charts are rendered in less than 2 seconds after any filter change is applied.
Performance is consistent across multiple test iterations.
regulatory_basis: General principle that software performance should not impede quality control processes.
Implied requirement from URS for system to be fit for purpose in a QC lab environment.
data_integrity_requirements: The performance test must not corrupt or alter the source data file.
The full dataset must be loaded completely for accurate chart rendering.
urs_requirements: URS-020-010: Load 100k data points in < 5 seconds on supported hardware.
URS-020-011: Render charts in < 2 seconds after filter changes.
